title: openai-compat: align tool_choice semantics, schema mapping and tool message formatting
author: Ethan Monroe
description:
Motivation: Bring Redwood's OpenAI-compatibility layer for function/tool calling into alignment with recent OpenAI semantics around tool_choice and stricter tool schema mapping. This PR fixes a number of inconsistencies that caused (1) incorrect selection when the model returned ambiguous tool_choice payloads, (2) schema mismatch exceptions for typed tool inputs, and (3) differences in tool message formatting between streaming and non-streaming code paths.

What this PR does: patch the compatibility layer and public API surface so that: (a) tool_choice is consistently resolved using the highest-confidence candidate, falling back to name matching when ids are missing; (b) tool schema mapping uses a tolerant coercion layer for primitives and returns clear validation errors for structural mismatches; (c) streaming calculator for tool messages emits the same tool call envelope and final message formatting as the synchronous path (including correct role, name, and content schema JSON); (d) adds unit/integration tests and doc updates describing migration guidance.

Implementation notes: key changes include: (1) compat/openai/tool_choice_resolver.ts: new deterministic resolver with confidence threshold and fallback rules; (2) compat/openai/schema-mapper.ts: centralized mapping code with a two-stage coercion + strict validation option; (3) runtime/streaming/tool-formatter.go: unify formatter to reuse the schema-mapper and canonical tool envelope; (4) sdk/* clients: small helpers to normalize tool call events during streaming; (5) docs/openai-compat.md: updated section on tool_choice, example payloads, and migration steps.

Backward compatibility: default behavior preserves existing behavior when feature-flag 'openai_compat_strict_tool_schema' is false. When enabled, callers will receive validation errors earlier (400s) for schema mismatches; migration notes are in docs/openai-compat.md.

Testing: added 28 unit tests and 6 integration tests simulating streaming and non-streaming tool calls across multiple models. CI reproducer included for a previously flaky streaming test.

Related: ENG-2145 tracks compatibility gaps; ENG-2198 covers streaming consistency work.

Release notes: See release_notes field.
